tiers.impact: This is the inflection point, not just more of the same trend — completion %, ANY/A, and FG% all drop sharply above this line in multiple independent studies. Expect a run-heavier game plan, reduced effective FG range, and fewer explosive pass plays. Lower total scoring is likely, driven mainly by kicking and big-play suppression rather than the run game itself. detail: Mostly end-to-end: ~10 mph along the field, only ~0 across. Distance is the effect — kicks toward the north end zone go into it, toward the south end zone with it, so FG range and punt distance depend on which end the ball is going to.

Teams switch ends every quarter, so each side has the wind for one quarter of each half; the effect lands on 4th-down and FG decisions quarter by quarter (and on which end a team defends in the 4th) more than on one team's total.

tiers.impact: Sustained wind may look manageable, but individual gusts are what actually disrupt a given snap — elevated risk of a shanked punt, pushed FG, or badly thrown deep ball on any single play, even if the average reading looks fine.
